name: error-metadata-padded-base64
description: Metadata encoded with base64 padding is not base64url(no-pad) and is dropped as a non-fatal malformed field, exactly like any other unparseable metadata.
grounding: The metadata alphabet is base64url without padding, and it is the only accepted alphabet. A payload that decodes only under a padded or std alphabet is not conformant and is dropped.
notes: The bytes here are a well-formed JSON object ({"a":1}) under a padded alphabet, so this case does not test JSON validity — it tests that the alphabet itself is part of the contract. It is the case that separates a strict decoder from a permissive one that tries several alphabets before giving up. Both readings are individually defensible, which is exactly why the corpus has to pick one: a strict reader and a permissive reader handed these identical bytes produce different rows, and 'the same capture on two paths yields the same row' is the property the corpus exists to protect. Pinning no-pad here makes any permissive decoder visible as a deviation instead of as silent disagreement.
